name: In-process LRU
solves: Provides a high-performance least-recently-used map for a single Node.js process (npm package `lru-cache`) with TTL, size-based eviction, and fetch patterns — in-memory only, with no network backend.
best_for: Memoizing hot function results inside one process where a remote store would be overkill
Libraries and CLIs that need a tiny, dependency-light LRU with TTL
Per-process data that intentionally stays local to the worker
Bounding memory with max item count or max size limits
Synchronous get/set without async network I/O
skip_when: You need a store visible to multiple processes or hosts — use node-redis, ioredis, or Upstash
You need disk-backed or multi-driver storage — use unstorage or Keyv
Stampede protection and distributed invalidation are requirements
You are solving multi-instance application caching — start with Redis or Upstash, not an in-process LRU
You only need a single Map with manual deletes and no eviction policy
